## Purpose

This SOP covers the safe use, storage, disposal, and spill treatment of
hazardous materials. It applies to staff, students, and researchers who
use acid, base, explosive, caustic, and poisonous materials in EA
Program laboratories.

This document does not explicitly cover radioactive materials.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All staff, students, and researchers handling
  hazardous chemicals in EA Program laboratories
- **Does not apply to:** Radioactive materials (see separate
  procedures)
- **Location:** SGM 133 and associated EA Program laboratory spaces


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure training compliance     |
| Trained Personnel | Follow this SOP, report deviations          |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## Definitions

- **Caustic chemicals:** Chemicals such as ammonium hydroxide,
  potassium hydroxide, and sodium hydroxide that are able to burn or
  corrode organic tissue by chemical action.
- **Combustible liquid:** A liquid with a flashpoint at or above 60 °C
  (140 °F); can burn at temperatures usually above normal working
  temperatures.
- **Corrosive chemicals:** Strong acids and bases, dehydrating agents,
  nonmetal chlorides, and halogens that are health hazards and can
  damage skin, eyes, and respiratory tissue on contact. Store
  corrosives under the fume hood on low shelving or in approved
  storage cabinets. Gas cylinders should not be stored in the same
  cabinet with corrosive liquids. Segregate acids from bases and
  oxidizing acids from organic acids; separate nitric acid from all
  other acids.
- **Flammable liquid:** A liquid with a flashpoint below 60 °C
  (140 °F) that can ignite easily at normal working temperatures.
- **Hazardous material:** Any substance posing a physical or health
  hazard as defined by OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200, including flammables,
  corrosives, oxidizers, toxins, and carcinogens [@osha1910].
- **Safety Data Sheet (SDS):** A standardized document describing a
  chemical's hazards, safe handling, storage, disposal, and emergency
  response procedures; located on the counter near the east entrance
  and at the PPE shelves in SGM 133.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Acids, bases, flammables, oxidizers, and toxic
  reagents are used routinely in EA Program labs.
- **Physical:** Glassware breakage, heat from hot plates and ovens,
  compressed gas cylinders.
- **Biological:** Soil and water samples may contain pathogens.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses / goggles
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Face shield (concentrated acids and bases)

### Required Training

- [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
  before handling any hazardous chemical


## General Safe Handling Procedures

### Working with Hazardous Materials

- Read the SDS for every chemical before first use.
- Never work alone when handling concentrated acids, bases, or
  flammables.
- Use the fume hood when working with volatile, toxic, or corrosive
  chemicals.
- Cap unused containers immediately; return chemicals to designated
  storage after use.
- Purchase the smallest quantity needed; order corrosives in
  plastic-coated containers where available.

### Physical Hazards

**Glassware:** Inspect glassware for cracks before use. Use extreme
care when inserting glass tubing into stoppers. Use heat-resistant
gloves near hot glassware.

**Burns:** Use hot plates or water baths instead of open flames. Tie
up loose hair and wear snug-fitting, non-synthetic clothing when
possible. Always use a fume hood with volatile organic compounds.

**Chemical spills:** Read the SDS before working with any hazardous
chemical. Always wear PPE, cap unused chemical containers, and use
fume hoods. Never work alone.

**Mercury spills:** Follow the college's emergency instructions for
mercury spill response.

**Explosions:** Develop written protocols for explosive chemicals. Use
fume hoods; avoid experiments in closed containers; always wear PPE.

**Chemical inhalation:** Never breathe deeply from a chemical mixture.
Use a fume hood; consider gas monitoring equipment for experiments that
generate toxic gases.


## Chemical Storage

### General Rules

- Store chemicals by hazard class, not alphabetically.
- Never store chemicals on the floor; use low shelves or cabinets with
  front lips.
- Secure shelves to the wall. Ensure shelves have lips to prevent
  containers from falling.

### Storage by Hazard Class

| Hazard Class       | Storage Location                              |
|:-------------------|:----------------------------------------------|
| Flammable liquids  | Flammable-storage cabinet (yellow, self-closing) |
| Corrosive acids    | Acid cabinet under fume hood (separate from bases) |
| Corrosive bases    | Base cabinet under fume hood (separate from acids) |
| Oxidizers          | Separate from flammables and organics         |
| Toxics / reagents  | General chemical shelves, secured             |
| Compressed gases   | Chained to wall; away from corrosives         |
| Refrigerated       | Lab refrigerator (no food); door labeled      |


## Waste Disposal

See [SOP-L006 Waste Disposal](SOP-L006-waste-disposal.qmd) for the
complete waste classification and disposal procedures. Key rules:

- Segregate waste by chemical compatibility (acids, bases, halogenated
  solvents, non-halogenated solvents, heavy metals).
- Label every waste container with the chemical name, hazard class, and
  accumulation start date.
- Never pour hazardous chemicals down the drain without verifying
  local discharge limits.
- Schedule EH&S pickup when a container reaches 75% capacity or after
  270 days of accumulation, whichever comes first.

## Training Record

Training is documented in EA Program files. Before working
independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Review SDS forms for all chemicals to be handled
4. Demonstrate understanding of spill response procedures
5. Be signed off by the PI or Chemical Safety Officer
